item.title: Family of Renee Good files civil suits against federal government
item.description: Civil lawsuits are now filed against the federal government on behalf of the family of Renee Good, the 37-year-old woman fatally shot in January by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer in south Minneapolis.

item.title: Trump renews threat to resume attacks on Iran after U.S. midterms
item.description: Trump says he doesn't believe "you could ever have peace" with Iran, and renews his threat to resume U.S. attacks after the midterms.

item.title: Expert aviator reacts to FlyDubai incident
item.description: A pilot allegedly stabbed the co-pilot on a FlyDubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, officials say. Former National Transportation Safety Board chairman Robert Sumwalt breaks down his thoughts on the incident.

item.title: Supreme Court to hear dispute over Trump's mandatory detention policy
item.description: The Supreme Court said it will consider whether the Trump administration can detain tens of thousands of immigrants without access to bond hearings.

item.title: Trump deflects on audio of Paxton calling GOP convention a drag on polls
item.description: Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton reportedly told donors that "everybody's numbers are down" after a midterm convention in Dallas that touted both Paxton's campaign and President Trump's record.

item.title: Could Lady Gaga be "The Cure" for a Japanese convenience store's labor shortage?
item.description: Lady Gaga is teaming up with Japanese convenience chain FamilyMart to recruit for the short-staffed company. Japan faces labor shortages nationwide as the workforce ages. CBS News' Anna Coren reports.

item.title: Tennessee cancels executions after Christa Pike survives botched injection
item.description: Tennessee canceled its remaining scheduled execution this year after Christa Pike, the only woman on its death row, survived two doses of a botched lethal injection. A witness said she was "clearly very alive."

item.title: Pakistani airstrikes kill 10 civilians in Afghanistan, U.N. mission says
item.description: Pakistan says airstrikes in Afghanistan killed 22 terrorists, but Afghanistan's Taliban regime and the U.N. mission in the country say mostly children were killed.

item.title: Details emerge in case of former Cornell student alleging rape by frat members
item.description: A woman, identified only as Jane Doe, alleges she was gang-raped by seven fraternity members in 2024 and accuses Cornell University of failing to protect her.

item.title: Vance ramps up midterm campaigning efforts
item.description: Vice President JD Vance is campaigning ahead of Election Day. CBS News' Cristian Benavides explains.

item.title: Cornell Jane Doe said accused rapists knew she was intoxicated in statement to campus police
item.description: In a 2024 statement to Cornell University campus police, Jane Doe says that her accused abusers knew she was intoxicated. CBS News' Tom Hanson and Lilia Luciano have more details on this case.

item.title: Trump heads to Texas to campaign despite leaked Ken Paxton audio
item.description: President Trump will be in Texas on Thursday campaigning for Senate hopeful Ken Paxton, despite recently leaked audio where Paxton said he thinks Mr. Trump's GOP midterm convention may have hurt his chances. Ed O'Keefe reports.

item.title: Disturbing details on alleged Cornell rape victim's sworn statement
item.description: More disturbing details are coming to light from the alleged Cornell rape victim's official sworn statement obtained by CBS News. Tom Hanson reports.

item.title: U.S. surrogate for Chinese billionaire says she trusted agency, as questions arise
item.description: The CEO of the surrogacy agency Patriot Conceptions says he was unaware billionaire Xu Bo was building a massive family.

item.title: FlyDubai passenger recounts cockpit chaos: "I hugged my two boys"
item.description: Hila Evron, one of the travelers who witnessed the mayhem on the FlyDubai flight from Dubai to Israel, tells "CBS Mornings" about the cockpit stabbing.

item.title: 2 dead, 2 injured, 1 missing after Catalina Island helicopter crash
item.description: Rescue crews rushed to the Catalina Island coastline after a helicopter crashed in the ocean on Wednesday night.

item.title: Details emerge on midair mayhem after pilot was allegedly stabbed by co-pilot
item.description: Passengers on a FlyDubai flight headed from Dubai to Israel jumped into action Wednesday and subdued the plane's co-pilot after he allegedly stabbed the pilot. Imtiaz Tyab reports.

item.title: Christa Pike still alive after two botched lethal injection doses
item.description: Christa Pike, who was supposed to the first woman executed by Tennessee in more than 200 years, is still alive after two botched doses during a lethal injection. Skyler Henry reports.

item.title: Witness describes Christa Pike's movements after botched lethal injection
item.description: Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike survived a failed attempt at a lethal injection execution, her legal team says. CBS News' Skyler Henry reports.

item.title: Netanyahu says it's too early to determine motive in cockpit stabbing
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu indicated to CBS News that the motive of the Flydubai co-pilot accused of stabbing his fellow pilot on a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv is still unknown.

item.title: Co-pilot stabs captain, tries to crash FlyDubai flight en route to Israel
item.description: Israel leader Benjamin Netanyahu says the FlyDubai co-pilot who allegedly stabbed the captain and tried to crash the plane had undergone "Islamist radical indoctrination."

item.title: Can states try to regulate AI technology? A lawyer says yes.
item.description: Florida's Republican attorney general wants to stop OpenAI from developing its artificial intelligence products until a court determines they are safe. University of Florida law professor Derek Bambauer weighs in.

item.title: Protests in France as students demand better school conditions
item.description: Student protestors in France are demanding better conditions for overcrowded and underfunded schools. French Prime Minister Emmanuel Macron is calling for calm amid reports of violence. CBS News' Leigh Kiniry has more details.

item.title: Man who helped subdue pilot in FlyDubai cockpit incident speaks out
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says it's too early to tell exactly why one of the co-pilots on a FlyDubai flight to Tel Aviv allegedly attacked the other. CBS News' Dov Lieber reports, plus Aaron Navarro has more on President Trump's reaction.

item.title: Why Trump is campaigning in reliably red states ahead of the midterms
item.description: President Trump is hitting the campaign trail ahead of Election Day. CBS News political director Fin Gómez reports.

item.title: Ex-Arizona frat leader gets jail time after pledge died of alcohol poisoning
item.description: A former Northern Arizona University fraternity leader, Carter Eslick, was sentenced to two months in jail for his role in a hazing that led to the death of a pledge.

item.title: Where the Trump administration's lawsuits seeking voter data stand
item.description: The Justice Department has filed lawsuits against 30 states and the District of Columbia in an effort to force them to hand over their unredacted voter rolls containing voters' sensitive information.

item.title: Whale sinks yacht in South Pacific, sailors rescued alive 18 hours later
item.description: A sperm whale cracked the hull of a yacht sailing off New Zealand, forcing four sailors into a day-and-night fight for survival on the high seas.

item.title: Cornell agrees to independent probe of alleged rape case, Hochul says
item.description: Cornell University has agreed to hire outside counsel to conduct an independent investigation into the 2024 alleged gang rape case, Gov. Kathy Hochul says.

item.title: In Conversation with Sylvester Stallone | CBS Sunday Morning at 92Y
item.description: Correspondent Tracy Smith talks with three-time Academy Award nominee Sylvester Stallone before a live audience at the 92nd Street Y in New York City.
